00060 /**
00061  * @brief HxMessage Delivery
00062  *
00063  * These constants define how the messages are delivered: synchronously, or asynchronously.
00064  * Asynchronous message handling requires that an eventloop be running.
00065  * Synchronous message handling does not require an eventloop, however the message callbacks
00066  * are triggered in the context of the underlying thread. This control is used with IPC
00067  * and timer message handling.
00068  *
00069  */
00070 typedef enum  HxMessageDelivery_t {
00071     kHxAsyncMessageDelivery        = 0x0001,       /**< Messages are delivered asynchronously */
00072     kHxSyncMessageDelivery         = 0x0002        /**< Messages are delivered synchronously */
00073 } HxMessageDelivery_t;

00204 /**
00205  * @brief               Sets the IPC Message delivery system
00206  *
00207  * This function defines the delivery system the listener will use for delivering IPC messages.
00208  * There are two kinds, asynchronous (default), and synchronous delivery. The asynchronous delivery
00209  * will deliver incoming IPC messages asynchronously. This requires an event loop to run in the system.
00210  * Asynchronous messages handling makes it possible to handle incoming IPC messages inside the gui thread
00211  * or any other thread running the event loop. 
00212  * Synchronous IPC messaging will immediately trigger message callbacks. There's no need for an 
00213  * event loop to run. However, the message callbacks trigger in the same thread as the underlying IPC
00214  * messaging implementation.
00215  * Note that you cannot change the IPC Message delivery system of the default listener.  The default
00216  * listener will always deliver IPC Messages asynchronously.
00217  *
00218  * @param pListener             IN:     Valid listener. 
00219  * @param system                IN:     Message delivery system.
00220  *
00221  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful. 
00222  *
00223  **/
00224 HxResult HxMessageSetIPCDelivery(HxMessageListener_t* pListener, HxMessageDelivery_t system);
00225 
00226 /**
00227  * @brief               Sets the Timer delivery system
00228  *
00229  * This function defines the delivery system the listener will use for delivering timer messages.
00230  * There are two kinds, asynchronous (default), and synchronous delivery. The asynchronous delivery
00231  * will deliver timer messages asynchronously. This is the default behavior. It assumes there is an event loop running.
00232  * Asynchronous messages handling makes it possible to handle incoming timer messages inside the gui thread
00233  * or any other thread running the event loop. 
00234  * Synchronous timer messaging will trigger message callbacks immediately. There's no need for an event loop
00235  * to run. However, the message callbacks trigger in the same thread as the underlying timer scheduler.
00236  * Note that you cannot change the Timer Message delivery system of the default listener.  The default
00237  * listener will always deliver Timer Messages asynchronously.
00238  *
00239  * @param pListener             IN:     Valid listener. 
00240  * @param system                IN:     Message delivery system.
00241  *
00242  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful. 
00243  *
00244  **/
00245 HxResult HxTimerSetDelivery(HxMessageListener_t* pListener, HxMessageDelivery_t system);

00309 /**
00310  * @brief               Set the message data
00311  *
00312  * This function sets the message data fields inside the message instance. 
00313  * Note that the data is not copied when using HxSendMessage, but is copied
00314  * when using HxPostMessage. In the case of IPC messages, the data is copied
00315  * into a shared memory segment and each receiver will get access to this 
00316  * shared memory segment that is then freed when the last receiver has received
00317  * the message.
00318  *
00319  * It is the responsibility of the client to manage and free the actual data.
00320  *
00321  * @param pMessage              IN:     Valid message
00322  * @param pData                 IN:     Pointer to the data
00323  * @param size                  IN:     Size of the data.
00324  *
00325  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful. 
00326  *                              If size is bigger than the property
00327                                 kHxPropertyMessageMaxDataSize, then
00328                                 HX_RESOURCE_TOO_BIG is returned.
00329  *
00330  **/
00331 HxResult HxMessageSetData(HxMessage_t* pMessage, void* pData, unsigned int size);
00332

00435 /**
00436  * @brief               Send a message synchronously
00437  *
00438  * This function sends a message synchronously. If the message has an internal
00439  * range, any callbacks are triggered immediately in the context of the calling
00440  * thread. Therefore, HxMessageSend should only be used for internal messages if
00441  * the receiver can safely be called from the same thread as the sender. Note
00442  * that HxMessagePost should generally be used if the sender is not running in
00443  * the context of the default user interface thread as any receiver who accesses
00444  * user interface elements must be called in the context of the default user
00445  * interface thread. If the message has an external range, HxMessageSend should
00446  * always be used. In fact, a call to HxMessagePost for an external message will
00447  * automatically be converted into a call to HxMessageSend. Using HxMessageSend
00448  * for external messages ensures that the IPC mechanism is immediately
00449  * triggered. The thread in which any callbacks are triggered is determined by
00450  * each individual receiver through HxMessageSetIPCDelivery. The sender has no
00451  * control over which thread the callbacks are called from.
00452  *
00453  * @param pBroadcaster          IN:     Valid broadcaster or NULL for default broadcaster 
00454  * @param pMessage              IN:     Valid message 
00455  * @param senderID              IN:     Sender ID
00456  *
00457  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful. 
00458  *
00459  **/
00460 HxResult HxMessageSend(const HxMessageBroadcaster_t* pBroadcaster, 
00461                         HxMessage_t* pMessage, HxMessageSenderID_t senderID);
00462 
00463 /**
00464  * @brief               Post a message asynchronously
00465  *
00466  * This function posts a message asynchronously. If the message has an internal
00467  * range, the message is queued and any callbacks are triggered later in the
00468  * context of the process's default user interface thread. This is useful in
00469  * situations where the receiver must be called in the context of the process's
00470  * default user interface thread to ensure that data is not accessed by more
00471  * than one thread in the process. This function should not be used for messages
00472  * with an external range. For external messages, the thread in which the
00473  * callbacks are triggered is determined by each individual receiver through
00474  * HxMessageSetIPCDelivery. The sender has no control over which thread the
00475  * callbacks are called from. A call to HxMessagePost for an external message
00476  * will automatically be converted into a call to HxMessageSend.
00477  *
00478  * @param pBroadcaster          IN:     Valid broadcaster or NULL for default broadcaster
00479  * @param pMessage              IN:     Valid message 
00480  * @param senderID              IN:     Sender ID
00481  *
00482  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful. 
00483  *
00484  **/
00485 HxResult HxMessagePost(const HxMessageBroadcaster_t* pBroadcaster, 
00486                         HxMessage_t* pMessage, HxMessageSenderID_t senderID);
00487

00580 /**
00581  * @brief               Remove a specific Message Listener callback 
00582  *
00583  * This function will remove a specific callback that was originally installed for listening
00584  * to messages. This will free up the resources. It is the responsibility of the client to 
00585  * free any data associated with the callback.
00586  * 
00587  * Use sender ID of 0 in case you are not removing a callback targeted to a specific senderID
00588  * used by ListenToMessageFrom(). Otherwise specify the senderID used in this function.
00589  *
00590  * Note that all callbacks with the same address are removed from the listeners, in other words
00591  * if you installed the same callback listener multiple times listening for a specific message
00592  * class and ID, all these callback nodes will be removed.
00593  * 
00594  * If the message ID is 0, then the callback is removed from any message ID it has been
00595  * been installed to. Note that passing a message ID of 0 is slow and inefficient as every 
00596  * installed callback in the process must be checked.  Therefore, the use of a 0 message ID is
00597  * discouraged.  If the message ID(s) associated with a callback are known, it is much more
00598  * efficient to pass the message ID(s) rather than use a 0.
00599  *
00600  * @param pListener             IN:     Valid listener
00601  * @param messageclass          IN:     Message class
00602  * @param id                    IN:     Message ID or 0 in case any ID is valid.
00603  * @param callback              IN:     Message callback
00604  * @param senderID              IN:     Message sender ID
00605  *
00606  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.

00611 
00612 HxResult HxMessageRemoveCallback(const HxMessageListener_t* pListener,
00613                                  const HxMessageClass_t messageClass,
00614                                  const HxMessageID_t id,
00615                                  const HxMessageCallback callback,
